steps.text: If the player is not wearing either Builder's boots or Carpenter's boots:

steps.npc: Watch where you're walking. You should really be wearing some regulation boots, you know.

steps.player: Yours don't look very regulation to me.

steps.text: The shipyard worker scowls and ignores your comment as they get back to work.
If the player is wearing either Builder's boots or Carpenter's boots:

steps.npc: Though you know what, those boots do look the part.

steps.player: Oh, well thanks! But you're not...

steps.npc: How about a brew? On me.

steps.text: It's not entirely clear where it came from, but the worker hands you a cup of tea.
If the player is not wearing either a Hard hat or Carpenter's helmet:

steps.npc: Mind your head! You should really be wearing a hard hat around these parts, you know.

steps.player: Doesn't that mean that you should be, too?

steps.text: The shipyard worker scowls and ignores your comment as they get back to work.

options.text: If the player is  wearing  either a Hard hat or Carpenter's helmet:

steps.npc: That said, that hat'll be protecting you pretty well. Looks like a good one!

steps.player: Safety first, and all that. But where's your...

steps.npc: You look like you could use a cup of tea. How about it?
No time to talk. Too much to do around here.

overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.speaker: Shipyard Worker (A)
overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.text: They say a good way of remembering it is that a ship can have boats on it, but a boat can't have ships on it.

overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.speaker: Shipyard Worker (B)
overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.text: But say you have a ship with lifeboats on it, and that ship starts to sink. If all the lifeboats are deployed, it no longer has any boats on it, so is it no longer a ship?

overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.speaker: Shipyard Worker (B)
overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.text: I suppose if it's sinking it probably no longer matters. Still, at the moment it does sink, you could argue that it very briefly stops being a ship and starts being a submarine.

overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.speaker: Shipyard Worker (A)
overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.text: It's not just boats and ships that have this problem. You also have orcas.

overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.speaker: Shipyard Worker (B)
overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.text: More commonly known as the killer whale!

overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.speaker: Shipyard Worker (A)
overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.text: Except by many definitions, they're not really whales at all.

overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.speaker: Shipyard Worker (B)
overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.text: What is it with things at sea being named so poorly?

overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.speaker: Shipyard Worker (A)
overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.text: To be honest, it's not much better on land. Think about trees. You've got oak trees, maple trees, and then you just have... trees.

overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.speaker: Shipyard Worker (B)
overhearing-the-workers-to-the-south.text: 'What's your boat made of?' 'Wood.' 'So like oak or...?' 'No, just wood.'
